title: Photosynthesis
text: Photosynthesis is the process by which plants, algae, and some bacteria convert light energy, usually from the Sun, into chemical energy stored as glucose. The process takes place mainly in the chloroplasts of plant cells, using chlorophyll and other pigments to absorb sunlight. The overall reaction converts carbon dioxide and water into glucose and oxygen, releasing oxygen as a byproduct. Photosynthesis has two main stages: the light-dependent reactions that capture energy from sunlight, and the Calvin cycle (light-independent reactions) that use that energy to fix carbon dioxide into organic molecules. Photosynthesis is the foundation of most food chains on Earth and the primary source of atmospheric oxygen.
